subject_max.unit: characters in the first line of a commit message
subject_max.source: long-standing git convention (git's own documentation suggests about 50; many projects use 72); written from memory
subject_max.note: convention; https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit suggests a summary line of no more than 50 characters and says it is not required; no primary source fixes 72

body_required_lines.unit: staged lines (added plus removed) above which a message needs a body
body_required_lines.source: mstack's own first setting; no outside source
body_required_lines.note: working value; no primary source states a fixed number

body_required_files.unit: staged files above which a message needs a body
body_required_files.source: mstack's own first setting; no outside source
body_required_files.note: working value; no primary source states a fixed number

large_file_mb.unit: megabytes; a staged file above this gets a warning
large_file_mb.source: mstack's own first setting; no outside source
large_file_mb.note: working value; no primary source states a fixed number
